hypotheses.justification: chartRing κ S is the integral closure of `Algebra.adjoin κ S` in the field L, so it is a domain, and tInvChart κ t = ⟨t⁻¹, _⟩. Suppose t is not transcendental, so it is algebraic over κ (the Fact t ≠ 0 is omitted, so t = 0 is allowed). (1) If t ≠ 0: t is algebraic, hence integral, over the field κ. By `IsIntegral.tower_top` it is integral over adjoin κ {t⁻¹}, so t ∈ chartRing κ {t⁻¹}. Then tInvChart κ t * ⟨t,_⟩ = 1, so tInvChart is a unit. Having it in the prime ideal 𝔮 contradicts IsPrime.ne_top, so `h` is false and the statement is vacuous. (2) If t = 0: t⁻¹ = 0 and tInvChart = 0. By hchartInv every element of the ring is aeval 0 f = algebraMap κ L (f.coeff 0), so every nonzero element is a unit and the prime 𝔮 must be ⊥ = Ideal.span {0}. The conclusion holds. So the new proof is: if t is transcendental, use the existing argument (eq_span_of_pow_mem with transcendental_inv); otherwise use the argument above. hchartInv cannot be dropped: with L = κ(u) and t = u⁻², chartRing κ {u²} = κ[u] and the prime (u) ∋ u² is not span{u²}.
